h.QR code: um quadradinho impresso que car: QR code: a small printed square that carries your review link. The customer opens the camera, points it, waits for the notification to appear and taps it. Free to create — you print it and put it on the counter.
h.NFC: um chip dentro de uma placa ou ades: NFC: a chip inside a stand or sticker. The customer brings the phone close and the review screen opens on its own — no camera, no framing, no tapping a link. It costs a bit (it's hardware), but it's a single gesture.
h.Importante: os dois apontam pro mesmo lu: Important: both point to the same place — the review box on your Google Business Profile. Neither one "filters" who gets to review, and that's how it should be. The whole difference is in the friction to get there.
h.Custo zero pra começar. Você gera o QR d: Zero cost to start. You create the QR for free in minutes and print it on a sheet of paper. If you're testing whether asking for reviews on site is worth it, start here — it's better than not making it easy at all. (We have a complete step-by-step guide to creating the review QR code.)
h.Familiaridade. Depois da pandemia, quase: Familiarity. Since the pandemic, almost every Brazilian has scanned a menu QR or a Pix QR. The gesture doesn't scare anyone anymore.
h.Funciona em qualquer celular. A câmera d: Works on any phone. Any smartphone camera reads QR. It doesn't depend on the phone having a specific technology turned on. (About NFC, the most common question is the iPhone: we explain it model by model.)
h.Menos passos = menos desistência. Esse é: Fewer steps = fewer drop-offs. This is the key point. Scanning a QR takes 3 to 4 actions: pick up the phone, open the camera, frame the code, tap the notification. Each action loses people — especially older customers or those less comfortable with phones. NFC is a single gesture: tap. Someone who gets stuck at "open the camera" doesn't get stuck at "tap".
h.Imagem melhor. Uma placa rígida no balcã: Better image. A rigid stand on the counter sends a different message than a printed sheet with a little black square. In salons, clinics and restaurants, that matters.
h.Durabilidade. Papel amassa, plastificado: Durability. Paper gets crumpled, laminated paper reflects light and fails to scan, stickers peel off. A stand holds up on the counter.
h.Nem NFC nem QR \"geram\" avaliação sozin: Neither NFC nor QR "generates" reviews on its own. Both just shorten the path to the Google screen. The customer is the one who reviews — and they review more when (a) they had a good experience and (b) you ask at the right moment, with a short line like "enjoyed it? leave us a review on Google, it takes 30 seconds".
h.E um aviso que vale pros dois: o meio de: And a warning that applies to both: the collection method doesn't change the rules of the game. Whether it's NFC or QR — never buy reviews and never use tools that filter who can review (so-called review gating, where only happy customers are sent to Google and unhappy ones are diverted). Google prohibits both practices and may remove your reviews or penalize the profile. The stand is there to make it easy for every customer to reach the same screen — not to choose who reviews.
h.Se você tem que escolher um só e o orçam: If you have to pick just one and your budget today is zero, start with the QR code — it's the lowest-cost way to stop losing reviews because it wasn't easy enough. If you get a lot of foot traffic, there's a line at your counter and you serve a varied crowd (including older people), NFC tends to convert better because it removes the steps where people give up.
The customer who loves scanning, scans. The customer who has never scanned anything in their life, taps. If the stand on the counter has NFC for those who tap and a printed QR for those who prefer the camera, nobody gets left out — and you don't bet everything on a single gesture.
